source.author: Hrvoje Beban
source.title: Dominikanski antifonarij Franjevačkoga samostana na otoku Badija kod Korčule: analiza rukopisa
source.read_scope: Publisher-extracted article text on printed pp. 176–177 and 180–181; not a full-article reading or inspection of original manuscript pages.
source.translation: Croatian interpreted with AI assistance; no independent translator has checked the interpretation.

tradition_control.reported_james: Beban names O beate Iacobe omnium corde as a St James Vespers antiphon and O lux et decus Hispaniae as a Magnificat antiphon in a Dominican antiphoner.
tradition_control.reported_mary_magdalene: The same study identifies Hec corde compuncte veni in Mary Magdalene Lauds, as the IV.156 catalogue describes for f.8.
tradition_control.scope: A separate historical witness described by the author; no original page comparison, exact adjacency, full melody or Swedish/Finnish identity inferred.

duplicate_office_control.reported: Beban describes the Annunciation office at the end of Badija X and the beginning of Badija XI, saying the latter office is identical; the two codices are complementary winter and summer parts.
duplicate_office_control.caution: The example spans two distinct physical volumes, not two duplicated chant copies proven within a single physical book. It does not show St James is repeated in either Swedish or Finnish material, and does not rule in or out the IV.156/Fr 10406 association.

conclusion: The selected chant combination can reflect a broader Dominican liturgical tradition, and duplication across a multi-volume set is documented. Neither point adjudicates the alleged overlapping physical fragments; a source-identified Finnish f.8 image remains necessary.
